records.name: Verde
records.summary: Studio Gang's 23-story, 254-unit rental tower at 1070 Bridgeview Way, the fourth and last Phase 1 building. Construction started March 2022, leasing began April 2024, residents moved in from June 2024 and the ribbon was cut September 3, 2024; 59 of its units are below market rate after a 2024 re-mix toward 90% AMI.

The repo's status.csv and milestones.csv date the opening ceremony June 24, 2024; the sources say June 21, 2023 (SF YIMBY, MVRDV). Flagged in the PR for the owner.

names: Pier 48 Sheds A, B and C
records.summary: A 1928-30 reinforced-concrete finger pier with two Tudor/Gothic Revival transit sheds around an open 'valley', the southernmost contributor to the National Register-listed Port of San Francisco Embarcadero Historic District. The Mission Rock entitlements call for a Secretary of the Interior's Standards rehabilitation (261,000 gsf of production, restaurant, retail and exhibition uses); its planned anchor tenant Anchor Brewing closed in 2023, and today the pier is leased to the Giants' China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and events.

records.notes: Pier 48 -- historic pier (two parallel steel-truss transit sheds, Shed A and Shed B, plus a connecting Shed C added 1937-38 at the bayward end; ~261,000-263,000 gsf total incl. bulkhead buildings, aprons, and 'the Valley' -- a 33,800 gsf open-air corridor between Sheds A and B, historically used for rail cars/cargo transfer on remnant Belt Line Railway spur tracks). Built 1924-1930 (bulkhead wharf completed July 17, 1929); a contributing resource to the Port's National Register-listed Embarcadero Historic District. IDENTIFICATION: this blklot has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll, but its real, surveyed shape (including the visible gap between sheds matching 'the Valley') matches Pier 48's documented footprint and location exactly when overlaid on satellite imagery -- confirmed, not approximate. Currently managed by Giants Enterprises as an event/exhibition venue (concerts, conferences, corporate galas) and used for interim parking/construction staging; full historic rehabilitation (required to follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards, entitled for light industrial/PDR/artisan food-beverage manufacturing/commercial event space/maritime retail) has NOT happened -- Pier 48 sits on an aging pile-supported deck over water (unlike the filled/raised Seawall Lot 337 next door) and needs substantial substructure pile repair and seismic work first. Anchor Brewing was originally slated as anchor tenant for a ~209,000-212,500 sf production brewery/taproom spanning Sheds A, B, and the Valley; Anchor closed in 2023 and its 2024 buyer confirmed it will not reopen an SF brewery, so that plan is dead. Recorded as 'existing' (a real, actively-used historic structure, not yet redeveloped per the masterplan) rather than 'complete' or 'planned'. LOT CORRECTED 2026-09-17: this row joined blklot 9900048, which DataSF's Assessor roll retired on 2020-06-12 (date_rec_drop) when Seawall Lot 337 was subdivided; the live lot for the pier is 8719A001 (recorded the same day, active), whose 27,493 m2 also takes in the pier aprons -- the Design Controls' 'Pier 48 Apron' open space (Section 3.6) is therefore inside this record rather than drawn separately. The retired lot's shape had IoU 0.86 with the live one and both contain DataSF's 16,913 m2 Pier 48 building footprint (sf16_bldgid 201006.0000016).

records.notes: Building G -- Visa Global/North America HQ, 13-story ~299,600 sf (283,320 office + 16,280 retail); Henning Larsen design, LEED Gold target; TCO Jan 2023, Visa occupancy Apr 2024, up to 1,500 employees (Port memo, Oct 2023; henninglarsen.com/projects/mission-rock-building-g). records.name: Historic Building 12
records.summary: The 1941 Navy-built plate shop and mold loft at the heart of the World War II 'New Yard' (248 ft square, Aiken monitor roof), the first and so far only Phase 1 building delivered under Brookfield's Pier 70 DDA: lifted about ten feet against sea-level rise, rebuilt by Perkins&Will and Plant Construction as a ground-floor market hall, second-floor maker studios and third-floor offices, and issued a temporary certificate of occupancy in January 2022. Held on a 66-year, $1-a-year Port lease; nearly 90% leased by August 2026, with General Catalyst taking the whole third floor.

open_questions: Bond amount and issuer for the CalHFA bond-recycling debt (and whether CSCDA or another conduit was involved): looked in the Port memo 10A, the four DA annual reports, the Chronicle (Oct 2023, Aug 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025), SF YIMBY, Hoodline; no dollar amount for the bonds is stated anywhere.

Total development cost: only Hoodline (Dec 2025, citing the Chronicle) gives '$50 million'; the Standard gives $670,000 per unit (105 x 670,000 = about $70M). The two figures are inconsistent and neither is from a primary document.

Temporary Certificate of Occupancy / First Certificate of Occupancy date: the Port memo says construction was 'completed in August 2025'; no TCO date found. The 2025 DA annual report (due 2026) is not yet on the SF Planning page.

Construction start: the 2023 annual report and press give the groundbreaking ceremony as Oct 12, 2023 (site permit issued Oct 25, 2023), but the 2024 annual report says Found Middle 'commenced construction ... in June 2024' and the 2023 report says the construction contract 'commenced in 2024'. Both are recorded; the June 2024 date is probably the DA-defined commencement.

Design review approval date: the annual reports list Block 7B as 'Approved by Planning Department, 1.5.22; Planning Director Memo dated 3.2.22'. The signed approval letter is dated March 2, 2022; the Jan 5, 2022 event is not otherwise documented.

Parcel: the design review memo lists parent lots 4175/017, 4175/002, 4232/001 and 4232/006; the repo's blklot 4232020 must post-date the Phase 1 Final Map (recorded July 26, 2022). No document in the corpus states the new lot number; 'Lot 10' appears on the LMS plan sheets ('Block 7B - Lot 10').

Land conveyance to Found Middle: the DA Housing Plan requires conveyance at no cost in fee or by ground lease; the approved Affordable Housing Conveyance Agreement (March 19, 2024) is not in the corpus, so fee vs. ground lease and term are unknown.

Lottery: the SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says a random lottery would be held later that month, while the May 2025 Housing Plan amendment exempts 100% affordable projects that receive no direct City money from the MOHCD lottery. Whether Sophie Maxwell is a 'City Financed Unit' project is not stated.
Unit mix as built: Swinerton (contractor's own material) gives 70/21/14; the 2022 approval gives 63/28/7 of 98. No City document with the 105-unit mix was found.
Hoodline (Dec 6, 2025) calls it a 'six-story building'; every other source says eight stories. Treated as an error in Hoodline.

records.summary: Port-owned shoreline land (portions of Seawall Lot 349 and Pier 72; the DEIR's 1.6-acre 'Port sub-area' piece between the Power Station and the Bay, site of a potential recreational dock) leased to California Barrel Company for 66 years under Port Lease L-16662 for public open space. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE ONLY -- digitized from an illustrative planning figure, not a surveyed record, then clipped to the real Port jurisdiction boundary on its water-facing side and opened to remove a spike artifact (see digitization_method). The corrected centroid falls east of the real Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels, consistent with a bay-side location, and area now closely matches the EIR's stated ~1.6 acres for this piece. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly tens of meters on the land-facing sides (still convex-hull-smoothed over the true shape there), but the water-facing edge is now a real boundary, not hand-traced. notes.why_no_real_parcel: This land has no Assessor's Block/Lot number at all -- confirmed directly in the same Draft EIR, footnote 1, p. 2-5: "The Port sub-area, and City sub-area described below, are not assessed properties, and therefore do not have assigned Assessor's Block numbers." It therefore cannot appear in DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset and cannot be joined via status.csv/blklot.
notes.regulatory_context: Prequel Park is the ~2-acre interim open-space project (BCDC Application 2019.006.02, a non-material amendment issued June 19, 2025; SF Port Commission Resolution 25-70, Nov 18, 2025, amending Lease L-16662 with California Barrel Company LLC) of which ~0.4 acres sits on this Port sub-area land near the future recreational dock. Construction targeted Q3 2026, public opening targeted Q3 2027 per the Port's Nov 14 2025 memo (Calendar Item 10A).

open_questions: BCDC amendment 2019.006.02: the repo's geometry file and data/milestones.csv say it was 'issued June 19, 2025'. The BCDC permit tracker gives June 19, 2025 as the date the application was RECEIVED and June 26, 2026 as the date ISSUED. The amendment document itself was not found on bcdc.ca.gov (2018-2019 DRB/Commission URLs now return 404; the tracker is an embedded table that could not be saved as text). Treat 2025-06-19 as application date, 2026-06-26 as issuance.

Port memo 10A is internally inconsistent: p.2 says construction start Q1 2026 / opening Q1 2027; p.4 says Q3 2026 / Q3 2027. Both are recorded; the p.4 dates follow the DBI-submittal sentence and are the more detailed statement.

No dated source confirms that Prequel Park construction has started as of 2026-09-17 (searched sfport.com, sfplanning.org, Chronicle, SF YIMBY, Potrero View, SF Standard, developer site, ICA SF). The geometry file marks the Power Station sub-area half 'under_construction' without a source.

The 'Spring 2026 SF development pipeline' listing ('Potrero Power Station - Prequel Park', developer FIFTH SPACE, scope demolition/grading/utilities/stormwater/landscaping) cited in the geometry file could not be located online; no URL is on file.
Lease commencement date and the recorded lease are not in the corpus; 'March 2087' implies a ~March 2021 start but no source states it.
Exact footprint of the ~0.4 acre on Port land: memo Exhibit 1 is an unscaled rendering; not digitized.

Whether the 2024 annual report's 'temporary activation east of Delaware Street and Stack Plaza' (Andrea Cochran Landscape Architecture, construction then expected Q1 2026) is the same project later branded Prequel Park with Heatherwick Studio is not stated by any source.
Planning temporary use authorization (June 2025): no case number or document found on sfplanning.org.

Port Commission minutes of Nov 18, 2025: item 10A passed on consent with no discussion or public comment; the minutes URL is https://www.sfport.com/media/10953/download?inline (the meeting page's 'm11182025.pdf' link returns 'page not found').

Area of the whole interim park differs by source: ~2 acres (Port memo), 2.5 acres (developer site), 2.75 acres (Chronicle, ICA SF), 'almost three' (Potrero View); BCDC scope 57,000-62,000 sq ft. Recorded separately; not reconciled.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 21 (Substation No. 5, relocated)
records.summary: A circa-1900 steel-framed, corrugated-metal-clad shop with a double-gable monitor roof (101 ft by 76 ft, 10,172 sq ft), the only surviving Risdon Iron Works building and the earliest steel-clad structure in the district, later Bethlehem's Substation No. 5. One of the three historic buildings the DDA obliges Brookfield to rehabilitate: a 66-year lease at $1 a year must be signed within a year of completing the building on Parcel E1 (Phase 2C), so no rehabilitation has begun.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) as of 2026-09-17 -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 21: position matches multiple independent prose sources (adjacent to Building 12, fronting Slipways Commons) and its combined size (734.96 sq m) is within 4.4% of the previously-cited 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) documented footprint. The match rests on position, size, and satellite corroboration, not an explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there). A small 49 sq m footprint ~9m away was not included -- see digitization_method. Superseded history: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-13 -- this building's rehabilitation has not started as of the most recent primary sources found (see regulatory_context).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel), cross-confirmed against ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-17 a long chain of diagram/prose-based approximations (kept below for history) -- see digitization_method. Originally three converging real-world sources: (1) 2011 Port RFI "Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan" map (sfport.com/sites/default/files/FileCenter/Documents/939-Pier70_RFI_3-2-11_web.pdf, p.7/11), a scaled map with real street labels (Illinois St, 20th St) showing Building 21 immediately adjacent to Building 12 near the historic core, annotated "BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED"; (2) Aug 3 2017 Port Commission memo (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Pier%2070%20Final.pdf, Exhibit F p.68): "Building 21 (Substation No. 5)... would be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast, and in its new location it would front Slipways Commons... sits directly next to the proposed new waterfront arts facility"; (3) D4D Figure 3.6.1 "Illustrative Slipways Commons Plan" (p.56/PDF p.72), a scaled plan with a real 0-50-100ft bar and "MARYLAND ST" label, captioned "the historic node of Buildings 2, 12, and 21."
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and sits on the same huge, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot (blklot 4052001) as Building 14 and other structures across central Pier 70 -- no distinct blklot exists to join for Building 21 specifically, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually (see digitization_method).
notes.regulatory_context: Building 21, originally Substation No. 5, was relocated on-site and is one of three historic structures (with Buildings 2 and 12) the Pier 70 Design for Development commits to rehabilitating per the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (Pier 70 D4D S6.6.1). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row marked it "complete," inferred (not directly cited) from Building 21 being grouped in the D4D's rehabilitation commitment alongside Buildings 2 and 12. A follow-up research pass found the Port's own 28-acre site page (sfport.com/projects-programs/pier-70-28-acre-site) describes Building 21's rehabilitation as still to come -- the page shows a rendering, not a photo, captioned "Rendering of Pier 70 Building 21," under a "Rehabilitation of three historic buildings" heading, implying a future vision rather than a completed project. This is corroborated negatively by the Port's own June 2025 project-update deck (sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/Pier%2070%20Update%20-%20June%202025%20v3.pdf), which documents Building 12 and Building 15's full rehabilitation histories in detail but never mentions Building 21 having been touched. Status corrected from complete to existing (see status.csv for this value's definition) -- a standing historic structure, not yet rehabbed, with no confirmed construction timeline.

records.name: Mission Rock Block C
records.summary: A future Commercial Mixed Use block on 3rd Street south of Building B, entitled for a 190-ft building over a 60-to-90-ft base with required ground-floor retail. Unbuilt: it is still part of the Seawall Lot 337 parking lot, and the Port declared the next phase financially infeasible in 2023.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see digitization_method): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco / Mission Rock Partners, adopted April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial Mixed Use only (no residential option) per the D4D's Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1) -- ground-floor retail required. Max building height 190 ft per Figure 6.2, confirmed exactly. Positioned south of Block B, fronting 3rd St to the west and the Shared Public Way (and Mission Rock Square beyond it) to the east. No construction-start source found -- still surface parking as of the most recent research pass (Sept 2026).

records.name: Mission Rock Block K
records.summary: The smallest development block, a Residential Mixed Use site on Exposition Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard next to China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry, capped at 120 ft. It was in the original Phase 1 but was swapped out for Parcel F in 2019 to bring about 100 more units into the first phase; it remains unbuilt.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence: every edge is a recorded DataSF lot line (the Assessor has not made Block K its own lot; it is still part of the China Basin Park lot 8719A005 as of the parcels fetch), and the Design Controls figure trace agrees with those lines within 1.3 m at every corner. Planned, unbuilt residential block (120 ft maximum height). ANGLE CHECK: check_geometry_quality.py flags a 12.3-12.6 deg corner here (its tolerance is 12 deg). Every vertex of this polygon is a real, recorded DataSF Assessor lot corner (see digitization_method) -- the deviation is the real lot's own shape (Bridgeview Way's paseo lot 8719A007 and the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 meet the park lot 8719A005 at a corner that is not exactly square), not a shear or a misread trace. Accepted; see docs/site-definition-of-done.md.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor lot lines (lots 8719A005, 8719A007, 8719A010, 8719A003) bounding the lobe the plan's Block K occupies, cross-checked against Mission Rock Design Controls Figure 6.2 (p.151) and the Block K standards sheet (Appendix p.198).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Block K's land is still part of lot 8719A005 (China Basin Park); the lot lines around it exist but the Assessor has not split K off. Joining status.csv to 8719A005 would show the park and the block as one shape.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential Mixed Use, fronting China Basin Park and the Pier 48 entry along Terry A. Francois Blvd. Max height 120 ft -- the lowest height limit of any residential block on the site, confirmed by the D4D's own narrative text: 'the shortest residential tower would be on Block K facing Mission Rock Park,' preserving sightlines/stepping the skyline down toward the water. Originally slated for Phase 1 (with A, B, G) before a real, Port-confirmed 2019 swap with Block F -- the sponsors proposed changing Phase 1 from {A, B, G, K} to {A, B, G, F} to accelerate ~100 more units (~40 more affordable) and create a four-corner pedestrian intersection instead of a linear one; an interim-parking-preservation rationale sometimes cited for this swap is not supported by any source found.

records.name: Mission Rock Square
records.summary: The neighborhood's planned 1.32-acre (57,626 sq ft) central park, an urban green framed by Blocks E and F with a lawn, a plaza with an interactive spray ground, a cafe pavilion and a tree bosque with retail kiosks; the Design Controls require wind protection, public restrooms and preserved water views. The EIR also allows a 700-space garage beneath it. Unbuilt: it lies within the remaining surface parking lot pending a later phase.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt public square) on the undivided remainder lot 8719A006. North edge is a recorded lot line (~0 m); the other three edges come from the Design Controls figure through a 0.7 m RMS transform (~1-3 m). Traced area 47,724 sf, smaller than the 57,626 sf the 2012 proposal gave -- see digitization_method. An interim plaza built with Phase 1 occupies the north part of this footprint today.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls, Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151) and Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); north edge is Verde's recorded lot line (8719C001), south edge is Block E's traced north edge.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this square -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this square touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Dedicated public open space (Design Controls Chapter 3, Section 3.3). Directly framed by Block F/Verde (north) and Block E (south), with the Shared Public Way (west) and Bridgeview Street (east) along its sides; Blocks C and I are one street removed. The Design Controls figure draws it at about 1.1 acres; the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel table gave 57,626 sf (1.32 ac) for an earlier, deeper layout.

records.summary: Phase 1 office parcel at 20th and Maryland Streets, entitled for roughly 350,000 gross square feet of commercial office over retail and underground parking; appraised in 2020 at $66 million for a 99-year prepaid lease, but Brookfield declined to proceed in June 2020 and no vertical development has started. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell ~11m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, leaving a strip of unclaimed vacant land between the block and the street -- consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors (see Parcel E1's digitization_method for the same root cause). The diagram itself (Figure 6.4.2) shows this block's fill running right up to the street with no setback, so extended the two south vertices by 11m (measured via satellite pixel-color transition to the real sidewalk, 3 sample transects) to close the gap, matching the diagram's own convention rather than re-deriving the whole transform.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial/life-science, 90 ft max / 6 stories per Figure 6.4.2. Current design (DES Architects + Grimshaw, ~356,000-365,000 GSF, for King Street Properties' life-science program) superseded an earlier (2019) Hacker Architects + Quezada Architecture mass-timber office design (~300,000-310,000 sf, billed as one of the largest CLT office buildings in North America) -- both designs are real, the mass-timber one was simply replaced, not fabricated. No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Whether the King Street Properties partnership is still in effect: the Port's June 2025 deck speaks of the life-science effort in the past tense ('prior to collapse of that industry') and the July 2026 Real Deal report describes a 300,000 sq ft office building, not a lab.
The Feb 2020 staff memo says Parcel A is entitled for ~350,000 GSF while Resolution 20-07's recital says ~240,000 GSF; which figure the DDA option actually carries is unresolved.

An earlier (2019) mass-timber office design by Hacker Architects with Quezada Architecture is recorded in this parcel's geometry file; the architects' pages returned 404/empty during this pass, so it is not restated here.
Construction cost estimates for the office building: none found.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel K North (PKN)
records.summary: The 1.5-acre former Port parking lot at 20th and Illinois Streets, sold in February 2019 to a TMG Partners / Presidio Bay Ventures joint venture under a Vertical DDA after a competitive offering, generating $24.2 million of land proceeds for the Pier 70 project. Planning approved a 65-ft, 245-unit for-sale condominium building over ground-floor retail (377,506 gsf, Handel Architects) in November 2019; as of 2026 it remains fully entitled but unbuilt.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)' and the '20th Street Plaza' open-space strip (data/manual/pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson), neither of which is built yet.

open_questions: The purchase price: the only figure found is the Port's '$24.2 million of land proceeds from the sale of Parcel K North in February 2019'; the executed Vertical DDA and the Budget and Legislative Analyst report attached to File 190055 were not opened.

No groundbreaking or building permit was found. Bisnow's June 2019 piece says TMG and Presidio Bay 'broke ground after recent purchase', which conflicts with the Port page's 2020-2021 design-and-permitting timeline and with the November 2025 Potrero View report that no Pier 70 housing has materialized; treat the 2019 claim as unverified.

Affordable housing on PKN: the 2017 memo calls the units market-rate and the 2026 report says condo projects pay an in-lieu fee toward the stand-alone affordable sites, while the Planning conditions reference Section 415 affordable units; the actual obligation is unresolved.
Unit and square-footage figures disagree between the Port page (245 units, 377,506 gsf) and the two developer pages (241 units / 411,273 sq ft; 275,000 sq ft residential).

No basis for an expected-completion date was found: Parcel K North was sold to a private developer in 2019 and sits outside the 28-Acre Project's DDA phasing plan, so no Development Agreement phase window applies to it; the only schedule statement found is the Port's November 2025 comment that development 'is currently delayed due to ongoing market feasibility challenges,' with no target date, and the developers' own pages (TMG, Presidio Bay, Handel Architects) give no construction start or completion date, so this record stays undated.

records.name: Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space (Waterfront Terrace / Slipways Commons / Waterfront Promenade / Pier 70 Shoreline)
records.summary: The roughly five-acre waterfront park system of the Pier 70 D4D (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons and Waterfront Promenade, Sections 3.5-3.7) plus the roughly 1,300-foot Pier 70 Shoreline (Section 3.8), to be built by the developer and owned by the Port. Phase 1 includes three acres of parks, but the DDA ties park completion to adjacent buildings and the Port's 2026 report says the Phase 1 parks will be built 'on a schedule that coincides with the delivery of adjacent vertical development', so none has been constructed.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE, AND KNOWINGLY UNSUBDIVIDED -- combines four D4D-named open spaces (Waterfront Terrace, Slipways Commons, Waterfront Promenade, Pier 70 Shoreline) into one polygon because no source found draws a boundary between them; do not treat this as a single named place. Total traced area (~4.0-4.3 acres before/after clipping) is a reasonable match to the D4D's own combined figures (a ~5.0-acre waterfront area covering the first three, plus part of a ~1,300-linear-foot shoreline) but is not a precise subdivision or survey. Programmatically traced from a diagram's fill color, not hand-verified vertex-by-vertex.

Together with Building 12 Plaza/Market Square, 20th Street Plaza, Irish Hill Corner Plaza, and Irish Hill Playground, these comprise the D4D's total nine acres of public open space (Section 3.4).

records.name: Crane Cove Park
records.summary: Seven-acre Port of San Francisco waterfront park on the former shipyard shoreline between 19th and Mariposa Streets east of Illinois Street, built around historic Slipway 4 and two gantry cranes with a pocket beach, lawn and Bay Trail link. Planned from 2011, built under a $17.8 million contract awarded to Gordon N. Ball in November 2018, and opened September 30, 2020 at a total cost of $36.7 million; the playgrounds and dog run followed on December 12, 2025.

notes.accuracy_caveat: HIGH CONFIDENCE -- real, community-surveyed OSM polygon (not a hand trace or estimate), independently confirmed via its own leisure=park/operator/wikidata tags. Its area (~6.26 acres) is somewhat smaller than the ~7-8 acres commonly cited for the park in press/Port sources -- likely because this specific traced way covers the core landscaped park and not every associated feature (e.g. the boat launch apron or beach edge); not adjusted to match the citation since the citation isn't itself a boundary.
notes.digitized_from: OpenStreetMap (way 853562207, leisure=park, operator=Port of San Francisco, wikidata=Q108550863) -- a real, community-surveyed park boundary, not a diagram trace.

notes.regulatory_context: Delivered under the Port of San Francisco's Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (2010) as the public-open-space component of the overall 69-acre Pier 70 site, distinct from and adjacent to Brookfield's 28-acre D4D redevelopment parcel this project's other Pier 70 features are drawn from. Centered on two restored historic shipyard cranes; includes a human-powered boating center and public waterfront/beach access.

records.name: Building 12 Plaza and Market Square
records.summary: The roughly 1.5-acre 'social centerpiece' of the Pier 70 open-space network (D4D Section 3.9): Market Square between Buildings 2 and 12 and Parcel D, the Building 12 entry plaza on 22nd Street, a Maryland Street platform for vendors and food trucks, and possibly the retained structural frame of Building 15. notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- derived from a real, street-polygonized city block (not a diagram pixel-trace), subtracting Building 2, Parcel D, and Building 12's own committed geometries. This is a deliberate departure from pure diagram-tracing: since Figure 6.4.2's own green fill didn't precisely reach the real (satellite-corrected) edges of Building 2 and Building 12, using the real block boundary instead better matches both the drawing's evident intent (this block reads as fully built-out, buildings plus plaza, no gaps) and the satellite ground truth. The block polygon's north edge stops slightly short of Parcel D's own north edge (~14m, since the not-yet-built '21st St (NEW)' isn't in real street data) -- unioned with D's own extent to avoid an artificial gap there. Area (~1.38 acres) is close to, but still a bit under, the D4D's cited ~1.5 acres for this named space -- the remaining gap most likely reflects the plaza's true extent continuing south past the mid-block passage (labeled '15' on the diagram) into the block south of Building 12, which is not part of this feature.

records.name: Pier 70 Hoedown Yard 3 (HDY3)
records.summary: The northern parcel of the PG&E-owned Hoedown Yard at Illinois and 22nd Streets, zoned residential under the Pier 70 SUD and D4D (65 ft) but not part of Brookfield's 28-Acre Project: the City holds an option to buy the roughly 3-acre yard from PG&E, subdivide it into three parcels and offer them for sale, with an Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District over the yard meant to fund Pier 70's affordable housing. No sale, developer or construction has been recorded.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's north edge had drifted 1.26m south of PKS's own south edge (both blocks were independently re-measured at different times and no longer shared an exact boundary, despite the diagram showing them as one continuous fill with only an internal divider line). Snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's south-edge coordinates exactly, closing the gap to 0m. RE-SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): PKS itself was found to be badly mispositioned (60% of its area was being silently clipped away against the real 21st St -- see pier70_pks.geojson) and was shifted ~25m south to ground-truth against the real street. Re-snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's new south edge to stay attached; area dropped from ~2,699 to ~1,508 sq m as a direct, expected consequence of PKS moving into what was previously this block's own north portion. This block's own south/diagonal portion (touching HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground) is unchanged. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'HYD3 too small relative to its peers based on drawing'): checked whether this shrinkage is a real bug (i.e., whether the same northward transform bias found on PKS/C1/PKN/Building 113-116 also affects this block's own south/diagonal portion, which would justify shifting HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground south too, restoring this block's diagram-implied size while keeping everything attached). Tested this directly: interpolated the real, official 22nd St centerline's latitude at HDY1/2's own south-edge longitudes (the nearest independently-checkable real street to this cluster) and compared to HDY1/2's current south edge -- found a clean ~14m gap with NO overlap, unlike PKS's 60% real-street overlap that justified its own correction. This is the opposite signature from a 'drawn too far north' bug: if the same bias reached this far south, HDY1/2 would itself be overlapping 22nd St, not comfortably clear of it. Conclusion: the 21st-St-row bias is local to that row and does not extend to this block's own south portion or to HDY1/2/Irish Hill Playground -- there is no evidence basis to shift them south to recover this block's pre-fix size. This block's current, smaller size is treated as the accurate, forced consequence of ground-truthing PKS (which shares this block's own north edge), not an unresolved bug. Flagging this conclusion explicitly per this project's no-fabrication rule: if a future source shows this block's own south/diagonal corners were independently misread (a diagram-reading error, not a bias-correction consequence), that would still warrant revisiting this specific block on its own.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel E1
records.summary: Residential parcel on Maryland Street north of Building 21, mostly 90 ft with a 65 ft north leg under the D4D, assigned to Phase 2C in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. Under the 2017 DDA the lease of historic Building 21 is triggered within a year after completion of the building on E1.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential, mostly 90 ft max with a smaller 65 ft strip along its north leg per Figure 6.4.2. No construction-start source found. Geometry here is a simplified bounding shape -- the real parcel has an irregular footprint around the historic Building 21 (mapped separately in this project) immediately to its southeast.

EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell well short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery -- 13m short at the SW corner, 25m short at the SE corner (a growing gap toward the east, consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors). Extended each south vertex independently by its own measured gap (rather than a uniform shift) so the block's south edge now reaches the real sidewalk across its full width, matching Figure 6.4.2's own convention of drawing blocks flush to the street.

names: Elevation Sky Park San Francisco (interim use)
records.summary: Waterfront residential parcel at 22nd Street and the Bay, 70 ft under the D4D and assigned to Phase 3A in the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan. Its D4D building has no construction record; instead Elevation XR, with Brookfield, is opening the interim Elevation Sky Park entertainment venue (three projection domes and a pyramid on about 165,000 sq ft, a five-year term) on 'Phase 2/3 sites' here, with the first public event on September 19, 2026.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block's boundary is a hand-traced D4D diagram parcel, not a surveyed lot; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade (see digitization_method for the transform's validation). EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell ~22m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, part of the same local scale error documented on Parcel A/E2 (parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors land short of their true extent). Extended both south vertices by 22m to reach the sidewalk. Note this is still the D4D diagram's original 'E3' boundary, not a re-survey of ESP's own real tent/dome footprint -- see the ESP-merge note below for that separate uncertainty. CURRENT USE, POST-LEASE FUTURE UNCLEAR (added 2026-09-17): this parcel is being treated as the site of Elevation Sky Park, a real interim entertainment venue confirmed to be under a 5-year lease (see regulatory_context) -- that part is sourced fact. What is NOT known, and should not be assumed, is what happens here after that lease ends: the D4D's original masterplan designates this parcel 70ft-max residential, but that plan was adopted years before ESP's interim lease existed, and no source found ties ESP's lease expiration to an actual scheduled residential construction start, or confirms the D4D's original boundary/use for this specific parcel will still be pursued unchanged by then. Do not read the 'entertainment' use here as a permanent reclassification, or assume 'residential' will automatically resume -- both are open questions. The parcel-level match to ESP itself is also still an approximation: a rendering (SFGATE, Sept 2026) corroborated the general siting (shoreline-adjacent, near the historic warehouse core) but is an unscaled marketing image, not a site plan -- ESP's real footprint may still extend slightly into neighboring E2/E4, as the pre-merge overlap analysis found.

notes.regulatory_context: D4D-designated use: residential, 70 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (no construction-start source ever found for that plan). CURRENT REAL USE: Elevation Sky Park (Elevation XR, in partnership with Brookfield Properties), a 165,000 sq ft interim entertainment venue (3 geodesic domes + a pyramid) under a 5-year lease, fully permitted through the Port of San Francisco, opened to the public September 19, 2026 ('Pier Play San Francisco'). Port materials describe it as an 'interim activation on Phase 2/3 sites within Pier 70 development zone' -- confirming it is temporary by design, though not tied to a specific successor project or date.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Placement of Elevation Sky Park on Parcel E3 is this project's own reading (merged into E3 by the owner's decision, per the geometry file): the primary sources say only 'Phase 2/3 sites' and 'where 22nd Street meets the Bay', which is consistent with E3/H2 but not parcel-specific. A Port license or permit for the venue, which would settle it, was not found on any 2025-2026 Port Commission agenda.
The opening date of September 19, 2026 is two days after this record's verification date and is recorded as expected; the Business Wire release itself could not be read (HTTP 403).
Lease or license terms (rent to Brookfield or the Port) for the interim venue: not found.

records.name: Pier 70 Parcel E4
records.summary: The waterfront arts-building parcel east of Building 21: excluded from the developer's purchase option, capped at 50 ft and five stories, and reserved under the 2017 DDA for a roughly 90,000 sq ft arts facility (with replacement studios for the Noonan Building artists) on a 50-year, $1-a-year lease once $17.5 million in private contributions is raised. The Port's proposed 2026 amendments would rezone it to allow housing if the arts facility proves infeasible.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Designated use is 'Arts' per both the D4D (excluded from the developer's standard parcel-purchase option as 'the arts building parcel') and Brookfield's own leasing brochure -- NOT residential or general mixed-use as sometimes described secondhand. Recorded here as 'mixed' only because this map has no dedicated 'arts' use category; treat the real designation as Arts. Max height 50 ft per Figure 6.4.2 -- the lowest of any parcel at Pier 70. No construction-start source found.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2)
records.summary: A six-story board-formed concrete warehouse of 1941-44 (256 ft by 77 ft, 98,804 sq ft) north of Building 12, one of the three historic buildings Brookfield must rehabilitate to the Secretary of the Interior's Standards under the Pier 70 DDA. It is a Phase 1 option parcel to be held on a 99-year lease at an appraised rent; a 2021 filing described about 120 apartments in its shell, Brookfield now markets it as creative office, and the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would have the developer assign its option and close escrow within six months of Board approval, with certain impact fees and special taxes waived. No rehabilitation has started.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- RELOCATED 2026-09-16 from an incorrect west-lot placement (see digitization_method) to Figure 6.4.2's own labeled '2' Historic Building box, in the same east-side node as Buildings 12 and 21. Programmatically traced from this legend color, not hand-verified vertex-by-vertex; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, consistent with this site's other diagram-traced parcels. The close match (85%) between this trace's area and Warehouse No. 2's documented 236ft x 76ft footprint is a good independent sanity check, but this is still a simplified rectangle, not a surveyed building outline.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Officially 'Warehouse No. 2' per the D4D (Section 6.6.1), a historic industrial shop structure, footprint 236 ft x 76 ft. Brookfield's own leasing brochure lists its use as 'Office' (creative office), ~100,000 RSF of leasable space -- roughly double a sometimes-cited '~50,000 GSF, Arts/Maker' description, which understates both its size and its actual designated use. No source found confirms whether rehabilitation has started; absent from the Port's own June 2025 progress update.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 102 (former Power House)
records.summary: The 1912 Classical Revival powerhouse on 20th Street between Buildings 101 and 104, designed by Charles Peter Weeks, which generated compressed air and distributed electricity for the shipyard and still housed BAE Systems' electrical service when rehabilitation began. Orton rebuilt it as office space with a mezzanine and a rear addition (about 15,300-18,000 sq ft) and subleased it to JUUL Labs for ten years; the current occupant is unknown.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself. This footprint's area (~1955 m2 / ~21,043 sqft) is roughly double the '11,266 sf' figure this project's own earlier research attached to 'Building 102 (former Compressor House)' -- that figure was not independently re-verified this pass, and could describe interior/leasable area rather than the full building footprint, or could itself be imprecise. Flagging this discrepancy rather than silently picking one number; treat the footprint geometry (real, surveyed) as more reliable than the previously-cited sqft figure.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4046001) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll. The real Assessor lot groups 5 named buildings into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: The former Power House, built 1912, part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as Building 101 (HPC packet 2013.1168E, Nov 26 2013 review). Per that packet, Building 102 was 'in fairly good condition' at the time and in use as the powerhouse facility. No confirmed real-world tenant identified by any source found.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters)
records.summary: The 1896 red-brick Renaissance Revival office of the Union Iron Works on 20th Street, by Percy & Hamilton, the oldest architect-designed building in the district; red-tagged when Orton took it on, seismically braced with steel columns and back in occupancy with a certificate of occupancy in June 2017. It was subleased to Tea Living (Tea Collection) and then, by sublease and later a direct ten-year lease, to JUUL Labs.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 104. Buildings 122 and 123 (two small one-story 'check house' buildings flanking Building 104, per the 2013 HPC packet -- 774 GSF and 400 GSF respectively) are NOT separately represented here or anywhere else in this dataset: no footprint of a matching small size was found immediately adjacent to this one, most likely because DataSF's building-footprint extraction merged them into this building's outline (or Building 102's) given how small and closely attached they are. Their combined ~1,174 GSF (~109 m2) is a small fraction of this footprint's ~1,080 m2 total, so if merged in, they would not meaningfully distort this shape -- but their own individual positions are not confirmed and are not claimed here.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4046001) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll. The real Assessor lot groups 5 named buildings into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: UIW (Union Iron Works) Headquarters, Building 104, a Renaissance Revival structure built in 1896 with a distinctive clerestory top floor, unreinforced masonry construction. Per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E), it was previously used as a naval hospital/medical office (WWII-era conversion) and was a 'red-tagged,' seismically challenged building at review time; rehab included demolishing demising walls from the WWII conversion. Part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. as Buildings 101/102. ~30,000 sf usable (likely gross floor area across multiple levels, not this footprint's own area). Now houses a confidential corporate office tenant, 300+ employees.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop)
names: Union Iron Works Foundry and Warehouse
records.summary: The oldest surviving shipyard buildings at Pier 70: the 1885-86 brick Machine Shop and blacksmith/boiler shop (113/114, joined by a 1914 concrete connector, 492 ft long) and the 1916-17 reinforced-concrete foundry and warehouse (115/116) beside it. Closed and red-tagged in 2001, they were rehabilitated by Orton Development with a buckling-restrained-brace steel system and public atrium, receiving certificates of occupancy in November 2017 (115/116) and April 2018 (113/114), and were subleased to Uber Advanced Technologies Group and Gusto.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprints -- high confidence in each piece's outline and in the group's overall position (confirmed to sit within Figure 6.4.2's own '113-116' box). Individual identification of which piece(s) correspond to Building 113 vs 114 vs 115 vs 116 specifically is NOT possible from the sources checked -- Figure 6.4.2 draws them as one undifferentiated box, and the 2013 HPC packet's textual description ('115 and 116 abut Building 113/114') does not give a precise position. Rather than guess, this feature represents the combined complex, consistent with how it is actually shown in the source diagram. The combined footprint here (~9751 sq m / ~104,957 sqft) is larger than Building 113/114 alone (~86,100 sqft per its documented 492ft x 175ft footprint) and smaller than 113/114 + 115/116's combined documented GSF (~95,000 + ~38,000 = ~133,000 GSF) -- broadly consistent given GSF can include multi-level floor area not captured by a footprint, but not independently verified piece-by-piece.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This parcel (blklot 4111004) has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll. The real Assessor lot groups Buildings 113/114 and 115/116 into one polygon with no further official subdivision -- this feature uses the real building footprints instead, matched to the specific area of the lot that Figure 6.4.2 itself draws as the historic '113-116' complex.
notes.regulatory_context: Union Iron Works Machine Shop and Foundry, Buildings 113/114, on the south side of 20th Street just east of Illinois Street -- 'one of the most valuable and most vulnerable historic resources on the site' per the 2013 HPC packet (2013.1168E). Two unreinforced brick structures (Machine Shop, built 1885, and Foundry, built 1886) joined in 1914 by a reinforced concrete connector; building-length skylights, rows of high arched windows; ~95,000 GSF, 492ft long by 175ft wide, ~62ft tall. Buildings 115 and 116 abut Building 113/114, constructed 1916-1917, ~38,000 GSF, 57ft tall, with 'unusual windows and monitor skylights.' At review time the complex was red-tagged and subject to an engineer's advisory of imminent collapse. Rehab by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) included demolition/relocation of later metal additions on the west and south facades, a new steel seismic system tied into the brick perimeter, and demolition of two minor eastern appendages (Buildings 23/24, ~1,500 GSF). Proposed for industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail, alongside Building 14, framing a shared ~45,000 sf courtyard.

records.name: Pier 70 Building 14
records.summary: A World War II double-gable corrugated-metal heavy warehouse east of the Machine Shop, framing the Historic Core's plaza with Building 2; the smallest of Orton's eight Historic Core buildings, rehabilitated with a new mezzanine and seismic bracing (certificate of occupancy August 2017) and subleased whole to Obscura Digital (The Madison Square Garden Company) for seven years from September 2017.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 14: position matches Figure 6.4.2's own label (39m away, the closest and only plausible candidate among the lot's other footprint pieces once 113/114/115/116's own pieces are excluded) and its area independently matches the previously-cited 16,315 GSF within 3%. As with the other buildings split from oversized Assessor lots this project, the match rests on position and size, not an explicit building-number attribute in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and sits on the same huge, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot (blklot 4052001) as Buildings 101/102/104/113-116/21 and other structures across central Pier 70 -- no distinct blklot exists to join for Building 14 specifically, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: Building 14, a basic heavy warehouse dated to 1941 (per the 2013 HPC packet, 2013.1168E) with approximately 16,000 GSF of space and a 66 foot height, sits immediately east of the Union Iron Works Machine Shop complex (Buildings 113/114/115/116), framing a shared courtyard with them per the D4D's rehabilitation concept. Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as part of the same 20th Street Historic Core project; proposed for the same industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail as its neighbors.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). open_questions: Construction start: none found. Searched the 2021-2024 DA compliance reports (the 2024 report says no market-rate building permits have been submitted), SF YIMBY through Sept 2026, the Chronicle (Jul 29 and Aug 3, 2026), SF Standard (Oct 2025) and Potrero View (Oct 2025). SocketSite (Jul 2021) said construction was 'slated to commence in 2023'; SF YIMBY (Mar 2021) said Block 7 construction was expected to start 'by 2023, with completion by 2026'. Neither happened.

Whether the July 2026 Chronicle line 'tallest residential tower would be permitted to reach 248 feet' refers to Block 7A: the D4D allows 240-ft highrise towers on both Block 5 and Block 7, and the amendment package also lets Block 5 flip between residential and commercial. Not confirmed for 7A specifically; the Planning Commission packet for July 30, 2026 was not in the corpus.

Unit count drift: 277 (press 2021) -> 325 (approval 2022) -> 319 (compliance reports' LBE appendix) -> 315 and '420' on Planning Commission slides (the 420 may be Block 7A+7B). Which figure a future permit will carry is unknown.

SF Standard (Oct 15, 2025) says Associate Capital 'will move on to constructing a 300-unit market-rate apartment building' next; the Aug 2026 Chronicle names Block 8 (342 units) as the next building, so 7A does not appear to be next.

Ground-floor childcare (6,000 GSF per DA Phasing Plan) is assigned to Block 7 in the compliance reports; the April 2023 childcare/HPP phasing amendment (docs/phasing_childcare_hpp.pdf) was not read for this record and may have moved it.
No cost, financing, general contractor or ground-lease information exists for Block 7A in any source found; the land is developer-owned (not Port), so no Port lease applies.

The 'Block 7A' / 'Block 7B' names are the sponsor's; the D4D treats Block 7 as one block with a single 240-ft highrise envelope. The repo's geometry note saying 7A/7B are 'informal press/developer labels' is consistent with the Planning documents, which nonetheless use 7A/7B as case names.

This polygon traces only the portion visible on Figure 6.2.3 itself as a simplified strip (not the full shoreline extent, and not precisely following the actual curving shore/site-boundary line, which was simplified to a handful of vertices). Treat as directionally correct but incomplete and shape-approximate. Same 15-25m positional tolerance as this site's other entries. Position corrected 2026-09-15 (12m uniform shift onto the real shoreline, see digitization_method) -- the strip's own curve/shape still was not independently re-verified vertex-by-vertex against the coastline, only its overall position. Second position correction 2026-09-15: re-traced directly from satellite imagery color (water vs. land pixel classification), not the diagram transform -- now an 8m-wide ribbon on the real shoreline, including the southern point/breakwater curve. Still simplified (does not capture the D4D-labeled strips full north-south extent beyond what is visible here) and the exact width (8m) is an assumption, not measured from any park-design source. NOTE 2026-09-16: this feature's own outer-shoreline trace turned out to substantially overlap the newly-added 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)' -- evidence (a Spring 2026 construction-pipeline document independently describing the same corridor as a '2-acre Waterfront Park') suggests both features describe the same physical shoreline strip: this one as the D4D's own long-term planning label, Prequel Park as the actual interim-construction project now underway. The overlap is expected, not a tracing error -- see Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)'s own digitization_method. Not merged into one feature since the two have different sourcing/status and either could be independently corrected later.

open_questions: The brief's note that the BCDC permit application 2019.006.00 was 'filed complete June 2, 2020 per ceqanet' could not be verified: the CEQAnet entries (2017112005/2 and /3) show only the DEIR receipt (10/3/2018) and Final EIR receipt (12/11/2019) with BCDC as a reviewing agency. The original BCDC permit document (issued July 2021 per the Port memo) was not found on bcdc.ca.gov; the 2018-2019 DRB and Commission pages now return 404. Only the tracker row for amendment .02 was found.

No design review approval for The Point was found after the Dec 3, 2021 submittal; every annual report through March 2025 says 'Under Review'. The added expected-completion milestone therefore uses Phase 2's overall window (2026-2031, SocketSite Oct 2020) for the park's larger South/North/West pieces, not a park-specific or Point-specific date.

Seawall/shoreline construction: the only statement is Landa's 'building the seawall a few years ago' (Potrero View, Oct 2025); the Phase 1 horizontal work (pile driving, deep soil mixing) was substantially complete May 2023 but the annual report does not itemize shoreline protection.
Area: 3.6 acres (D4D, DA, DEIR) vs ~3 acres and '1,000 linear feet' (SF Planning page only) vs 4.0 acres (IMP); the geometry file traces only the visible strip. Not reconciled.

The geometry file's 'Waterfront Park' overlaps the newly added Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area); the sources agree the interim park sits within the future waterfront open space, but no drawing on file shows the interim footprint at scale.
No construction cost or delivery date for the permanent park; the 3-million-sq-ft trigger is not dated by any source.
Port Commission Feb 25, 2020 minutes: the local file is the agenda text; the adoption of Resolution 20-12 is taken from the Nov 2025 memo's recital.

OSM also carries other, smaller/overlapping ways for parts of this same park (e.g. way 579664205 further east, and way 27369705); this feature uses the single most detailed, currently-tagged way covering the park's main extent along Mission Creek's south bank. A second pass could merge the full multi-segment shoreline extent. Updated 2026-09-20: now a MultiPolygon that also includes P1, P2 and P8's geometry (P1 a separate segment further along the same north/west bank; P2/P8 real scraps of land on the creek's opposite/south-east bank, not contiguous with this record's original OSM shape). Each sub-piece keeps its own sourcing/confidence as documented in its own original record (P1, P2, P8) -- this union does not upgrade their confidence to this record's own 'HIGH CONFIDENCE, real OSM' rating.

The Potrero View source's fall-2021 target (after a COVID-19 pause) did not hold -- the Landscape Performance Series case study gives an actual completion date of October 2022, about a year later.

No source checked gives Mission Creek Park's own original construction/opening date; the Mission Creek Park Pavilion within it has a separately sourced 2003 completion (data/records/mission_bay_creek_park_pavilion.json), but that doesn't establish when the surrounding park landscaping itself opened -- background reading (a Southeast Waterfront community history page, and a landscape-architecture magazine mention of a 2004-dated EDAW site-plan rendering found only in search-summary form, not confirmed against the actual article text) suggested an early-2000s completion but nothing specific enough to cite as a fact.

OCII's September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation (src-ocii-transition-2023) lists plan parcels P1, P3, P5, P6, P10, P11/11A, P16, P17 and P26 as already RPD-managed by that date, but lists 'P2/P8' among parcels RPD 'will manage ... when built' (i.e., not yet complete as of Sept 2023) -- this record's own geometry file separately documents a 2026-09-20 union with P2 and P8 as 'barely touch[ing] this record's original shape,' consistent with those specific pieces being a later, smaller addition rather than part of the original park; not used to date the union since the two documents describe different things (a funding/management list vs. a geometry merge).

OCII's plan-label usage for this park is inconsistent across documents over time: the Nov 2024 CAC deck labels the whole feature 'P3'; the current sfocii.org open-space page splits it into P1 (amphitheater), P2 and P3; and a 2015 Successor Agency LRPMP (cited on this repo's neighboring P7/P8/P9 records) uses P2, P7, P8 and P9 for nearby, separately tracked open-space parcels along the same creek. Not reconciled here.

open_questions: No independently published source dates when this specific stretch was built; it was hand-traced from satellite imagery because it was visibly already landscaped, not because any source dated its construction.

This record's own digitization_method log says OCII's plan labels P1 and P3 both fall somewhere in this general stretch, per that log's reading of the Nov 2024 CAC 'Remaining Mission Bay Open Space Parcels Update' -- but that deck's own extractable text only labels the whole wider park 'Mission Creek Park (P3)' and does not break out a separate P1 sub-area within this specific reach; which label (if either) applies to this exact segment, versus to the separately tracked Mission Creek Park record's own P1 (an amphitheater, per OCII's current open-space page), is not resolved.
Name/operator: presumed to be part of the same SF Recreation and Park Department-managed Mission Creek Park system as its neighbors, but not independently confirmed for this specific segment.

2026-09-22 pass, flagged for the owner rather than resolved: this record is currently classified 'Mission Bay South' (approximate_projects.csv) and its own sourcing leans on Mission Bay South's P1/P3 plan labels (see above). But this record's own coordinates sit at the same latitude as other already-tracked Mission Bay North records (The Beacon, Rich Sorro Commons), north of the core of the separately-tracked, South-side mission_bay_creek_park record. A landscape architecture firm's own project page (Munden Fry Landscape Associates, mflastudio.com/mission-creek-park-north) independently describes real, differently-numbered 'NP1 Mission Creek Park Promenade' and 'NP2 Mission Creek Park' parcels for Catellus, built 1999-2011, on Mission Creek's north bank -- a description (residential to the north, the creek and a houseboat community to the south) that matches this record's own traced bank. Whether this segment is actually part of Mission Bay North's NP1/NP2 system rather than South's P1/P3 is an open identity question bigger than a date, not resolved here -- flagged for a closer look, possibly including whether this record's site classification itself should change.

2026-09-22, new data point (not a resolution): re-running this project's own DataSF business-registration spatial join (src/join_retail.py, out/retail_needs_review_approximate.csv) after this record's geometry was added shows several registrations -- Buenafe #2, All May See, All May See Foundation, Simon Fung -- whose registered point-location falls inside THIS west building's polygon, but whose own listed street address is '490 Illinois St' (the other, east-of-Illinois-St tower's address), not a west-of-Illinois-St address. Notably, the same join's matches for the neighboring ucsf_bayfront_medical_building and ucsf_illinois_street_garage records DO show addresses consistent with their own already-sourced identities (520 Illinois St and 590 Illinois St respectively), which is corroborating, not contradictory, evidence for those two.

records.summary: A 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and maintenance facility at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square, including the existing 4th & King Street Station itself. Owned by Prologis, with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); Prologis has floated development concepts including roughly 2,500 homes, up to 4 million square feet of commercial space and a tower as tall as 850 feet, via a Development Agreement, the same approval path used for Pier 70, Mission Rock and Potrero Power Station.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- not a surveyed parcel or a GIS file from Caltrain/Prologis/SF Planning. The active rail right-of-way here carries no Assessor block/lot in DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset (checked directly; consistent with railroad right-of-way being outside the normal local assessment roll), so this could not be joined via status.csv like a real parcel. Three of the four sides (Townsend, 4th, 7th) are real, continuous DataSF street centerlines; the fourth (King St plus a straight closing line where King's real data ends short of 7th, at the I-280 interchange) is the weakest edge and the one most likely to need revision if a real project boundary or EIR figure becomes available. Includes the existing Caltrain 4th & King Street Station itself, which the project's own description treats as part of the site being redeveloped, not something outside it.
notes.digitized_from: Bounded by DataSF's official street centerlines (data/raw/official_street_centerlines.geojson): Townsend St (4th-7th) on the north, 4th St (Townsend-King) on the east, 7th St (Townsend-King) on the west, and King St (4th-~6th, where its real centerline data ends) on the south, each buffered by the project's standard measured half-width (src/street_geometry.py, 6.8m) and inset from the outer street-to-street ring by that same half-width to approximate the curb/yard edge rather than the street centerline itself -- same method as P9 (data/manual/mission_bay_p9_open_space.geojson). King St's real DataSF centerline stops short of 7th St (its last segment ends at -122.397986, 37.773324): that stretch of the site's real southern edge is not a city street at all but the I-280 northbound/southbound ramp interchange (confirmed both by the DataSF centerlines' own 'I-280 N/S ON/OFF RAMP' segments in the same file and by satellite imagery, which shows the ramp curving directly along the yard's southwest taper), so the closing edge there is a straight line from King St's last real point to 7th St's King-St corner, not a surveyed street. The resulting inset polygon is 20.08 acres, matching the SF Planning/Caltrain FAQ's own '20-acre site' description almost exactly, and its outline was checked directly against Esri World Imagery (via contextily) overlaid in QGIS-equivalent fashion -- it tracks the real fan of tracks and the 4th & King station platform canopy tightly, confirmed by the site owner 2026-09-21 after a side-by-side review of the overlay.

The 20-acre site at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square: Caltrain's northern terminus and an active service/maintenance yard, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. Directly borders Mission Bay North: OCII's own December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map shows the blocks informally labeled N5A, N6 and N7 in this area with no assigned land use and no drawn boundary (unlike every neighboring numbered Mission Bay North block, which has both), consistent with this still being active rail infrastructure outside Mission Bay North's own planned build-out as of that map.
